intro: A decision list, not a wish list. Each suggestion states what to do, why, what it costs, and what would make it a bad idea. Rows marked Shipped are live on this site; the three paths at the top say what order to do the rest in. Where two sessions proposed opposite moves — a seasonal page now (SUG-25) versus held (SUG-23), original drawings (SUG-30) versus generated scenes (SUG-27) — both rows stay, and the decision log says which one this build took.

statusKey.label: Shipped
statusKey.note: Already built on the live site in this pass.

statusKey.label: Recommend next
statusKey.note: Highest confidence, do this before the others.

statusKey.label: Consider
statusKey.note: Worth doing, but depends on an earlier decision.

statusKey.label: Hold
statusKey.note: Do not do this yet. Reason given.

statusKey.label: Rejected
statusKey.note: Would break a rule or mislead a reader.

suggestions.title: Keep the site in 'how to decide' voice, permanently, until products are actually tested
suggestions.why: The FTC forbids describing hands-on experience you do not have, and readers detect the fake version instantly. The reliable way to sound human without lying is to write about the decision instead of the verdict: what the drawers are like, what the counter cost is, who the machine is wrong for.
suggestions.cost: None. It is a writing constraint, enforced by the build.
suggestions.risk: A guide that never says 'we tested this' competes poorly against sites that can. That is a real disadvantage and it is the correct one to accept.
suggestions.decide: Accept. Every page already follows it.

suggestions.title: Split into two publications, or pick one category and go deep
suggestions.why: Three air fryers and two thermometers are two different buying moments. Search engines reward a site that owns one topic. A small site trying to own 'kitchen gear' owns nothing.
suggestions.cost: Splitting means two domains, two sitemaps, twice the setup. Going deep on air fryers means the thermometers get a single supporting page.
suggestions.risk: If the thermometer affiliate offers a better commission or a bounty, narrowing too early gives up real money.
suggestions.decide: Recommend: keep one site, make air fryers the front section, and treat thermometers as the accessory section — which is what the current structure already does. Confirm before adding a third category.

suggestions.title: Get PA-API or Creatives access before writing another word
suggestions.why: It is the unlock for the three things this site most obviously lacks: prices, ratings, and product images. All three are currently blank because the rules require API-sourced data. One credential fixes all of it at once.
suggestions.cost: Eligibility requires qualifying sales first — a chicken-and-egg problem for a new account.
suggestions.risk: None to the site. The risk is waiting on access and shipping nothing meanwhile, which is why the current build ships without it.
suggestions.decide: Apply as soon as the account qualifies. Track it in the questions register as Q-11 and Q-12.

suggestions.title: Replace the submitted short links with constructed Special Links (done); prove one works (blocked)
suggestions.why: The submitted links carried no visible tag and their compliance status is unsettled. Constructing amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=shopnow047c-20 is unambiguous, keeps the destination visible in the status bar, and satisfies the link-clarity requirement.
suggestions.cost: None.
suggestions.risk: If the tag is not enrolled, every link still earns nothing. That is the one thing this cannot fix.
suggestions.decide: Constructed links are live. The proof step is blocked: it needs the owner's Associates Central sign-in (FLG-024). Next step: click one link per product while signed in and confirm it appears in the tracking report.

suggestions.title: Publish on a real cadence: a new guide every week for eight weeks, then read the query data
suggestions.why: Question-shaped guides are the right shape, but five is not a sample. A weekly cadence for two months produces enough pages and enough query impressions to see which question people actually arrive with, which is the only way to stop guessing topics.
suggestions.cost: A substantive guide per week. Each needs its own verified spec pass.
suggestions.risk: Cadence without quality control produces the thin content the brief explicitly rejects. The build gate must stay on.
suggestions.decide: Adopted 2026-11-20 as the publishing cadence; see the decision log. A new guide every Monday (New York time) for eight weeks. Basis, checked on Amazon Associates Help: content should be "recent (generally within the last 60 days)" and "a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts" (FLG-013). Each guide is added to the sitemap and feed in the same commit and must pass the build and compliance gates. Measurement at week eight needs Search Console and analytics, which are owner-blocked (FLG-009, FLG-011); it is not estimated.

suggestions.title: Add a real author byline with a named person
suggestions.why: Unattributed buying advice reads as generated, which is precisely the failure the brief names. A byline with a short bio and a stated method is the cheapest credibility signal available.
suggestions.cost: Requires a real person willing to be named and accountable.
suggestions.risk: A byline attached to content the person did not write is worse than no byline.
suggestions.decide: Decision needed from the requester. Cannot be fabricated.

suggestions.title: Move to a custom domain before building any authority
suggestions.why: A /WinA/ subpath reads as a side project, and moving later discards whatever equity accumulated. Doing it now costs a domain and one setting.
suggestions.cost: Domain registration plus DNS. About an hour.
suggestions.risk: Slight setup friction with HTTPS and the CNAME file.
suggestions.decide: Recommend. The build already keeps the origin in one config value, so the change is small.

suggestions.title: Deploy the analytics collector, and accept that orders cannot be counted yet
suggestions.why: Click data is available today and is the fastest honest feedback loop. Order data has to come from Associates reports, which arrive later. Separating the two keeps the ledger truthful.
suggestions.cost: One worker deploy and a secret.
suggestions.risk: A self-hosted collector is a privacy obligation. The current design stores no identifiers, which keeps that burden small.
suggestions.decide: Recommend deploying to close FLG-011. Do not import a third-party tracker as a shortcut.

suggestions.title: Add a 'who should not buy this' block to every product page
suggestions.why: The single most useful thing a buying guide can say, and the thing competitors skip. It also converts better, because readers trust a page that talked them out of something.
suggestions.cost: A short block per product.
suggestions.risk: None. It requires actually understanding the trade-off, which is why most sites omit it.
suggestions.decide: Consider. The current pages carry a trade-off line; expanding it to a full block is the natural next edit.

suggestions.title: Build a real comparison table with measured dimensions
suggestions.why: The comparison page exists but is thin because dimensions are unverified. Counter footprint is the number that actually decides a purchase, and nobody publishes it clearly.
suggestions.cost: Researching dimensions from manufacturer spec sheets, with a source link per number.
suggestions.risk: A wrong dimension is worse than a blank. Only add numbers with a source.
suggestions.decide: Consider once manufacturer sheets are gathered. Until then the table shows what is verified and says what is not.

suggestions.title: Add a short 'how we choose what to recommend' block to the front page
suggestions.why: Readers arriving cold need one sentence on why these five products and not others. It also pre-empts the 'is this an ad' reflex.
suggestions.cost: Three sentences.
suggestions.risk: Can tip into self-referential process talk, which the brief explicitly wants kept off the front page. Keep it to a single block low on the page.
suggestions.decide: Consider. The About page currently carries this.

suggestions.title: Do not add a price tracker, price alerts, or a deal feed
suggestions.why: Prohibited outright by §6(y) regardless of how it is built.
suggestions.cost: Zero.
suggestions.risk: It is the most requested feature on affiliate sites and the most direct route to account termination.
suggestions.decide: Rejected. Documented so no future session builds it.

suggestions.title: Do not generate volumes of near-duplicate pages to chase long-tail queries
suggestions.why: Template-spun variants of the same article are the definition of the thin, generated content the brief rejects, and they dilute the pages that could rank.
suggestions.cost: Zero.
suggestions.risk: It works briefly, then gets the whole domain discounted.
suggestions.decide: Rejected. The build gate refuses pages without unique content fields.

suggestions.title: Hold the email capture until there is something to send
suggestions.why: Collecting addresses with no ESP and no publishing cadence means collecting nothing. The form is currently inert and says so.
suggestions.cost: Saves an ESP subscription.
suggestions.risk: Capture opportunities are lost while waiting.
suggestions.decide: Hold until SUG-05 produces a cadence. Then wire one ESP and one welcome email.

suggestions.title: Hold all paid search
suggestions.why: No bid is permitted on Amazon marks, and a new site with no conversion data cannot tell whether an ad is profitable. Advertising before measurement is guessing with a budget.
suggestions.cost: Zero.
suggestions.risk: Slower initial traffic.
suggestions.decide: Hold until the ledger has real click and order data.

suggestions.title: Publish a dated 'last checked' line on every product page
suggestions.why: Specifications and availability change. A visible date tells the reader how much to trust the page, and forces the site to actually re-check.
suggestions.cost: One field, refreshed on a schedule.
suggestions.risk: A stale date is a public admission of neglect. That is the point.
suggestions.decide: Consider. Pages currently record the observation date in the register rather than on the page.

suggestions.title: Adopt a written design brief and treat it as the single source for every visual change
suggestions.why: Without one, every page drifts toward the same templated look that reads as generated. A brief that states the visual system, the layout rules and the anti-slop constraints gives every later change a consistent target instead of a mood.
suggestions.cost: One document. The draft is on this page and can be adopted as-is or edited.
suggestions.risk: A brief that is too rigid produces sameness. It is a starting point, not a cage.
suggestions.decide: Accept and adopt the draft below as the working brief; the reader-polish pass of 2026-11-20 implements it.

suggestions.title: Replace generic visual defaults with an opinionated editorial type and color system
suggestions.why: A confident serif-display / sans-body system with a restrained palette and one accent reads as a real publication. Generic system fonts, blue-to-purple gradients and neon highlights are the most common tells of an AI-generated marketing page.
suggestions.cost: CSS and type work in the shared stylesheet.
suggestions.risk: Over-design can crowd small screens. Mobile-first and readable tables must survive the change.
suggestions.decide: Type scale, contrast and the art frame implemented as an additive reader-polish block in assets/css/site.css, above the original system rather than inside it.

suggestions.title: Vary page layouts; stop repeating the same card grid in every section
suggestions.why: Identical repeated card grids are a primary tell of templated generation. A strong editorial hero, a reading column for guides, and at least one non-card treatment per page read as designed rather than emitted.
suggestions.cost: Template work in the build.
suggestions.risk: More layout code to maintain; keep tables and cards accessible.
suggestions.decide: Category hubs now use a shelf list view, the front page alternates hero / router / card shelf / seasonal banner / guide cards / honesty line.

suggestions.title: Write in a concrete, human voice and ban filler phrases
suggestions.why: Generic marketing boilerplate is the other main slop tell. Specificity — named trade-offs, concrete numbers, a real point of view — reads human and is what helpful-content guidance rewards.
suggestions.cost: Editorial discipline. Add a banned-phrase list to the editorial standards so the gate can enforce it.
suggestions.risk: None. It is the same constraint as SUG-01, applied to wording as well as claims.
suggestions.decide: Voice pass on the guides added in this pass: named numbers, no filler, no verdict language; the claim bans stay machine-checked.

suggestions.title: Publish to a topic roadmap on a cadence, adding each new guide to the sitemap and feed in the same commit
suggestions.why: Catchy, question-shaped topics are the traffic engine. A fixed cadence plus a feed keeps search and subscribers fresh, and the build already adds each guide to the sitemap and RSS automatically — that was a requirement, not a convenience.
suggestions.cost: A substantive guide each week, with its own verified spec pass.
suggestions.risk: Volume without quality control produces the thin content the brief rejects. The build gate stays on.
suggestions.decide: Accept the topic roadmap below as the first batch of hypotheses, then let measured demand reorder it.

suggestions.title: Use topic clusters and deliberate internal linking, not standalone pages
suggestions.why: A cluster (pillar + related guides + product pages) gives each page something to rank for and something natural to link to, and concentrates topical authority instead of spreading it across unrelated pages.
suggestions.cost: An internal-link pass on each new guide.
suggestions.risk: Over-linking looks manipulative. Keep links natural and reader-serving.
suggestions.decide: Consider. Design the cluster map before writing the second batch.

suggestions.title: Hold seasonal topics until measured demand exists
suggestions.why: Choosing December topics from instinct is exactly the failure FLG-020 warns against. Seasonality is a measurement, and there is no query data yet.
suggestions.cost: Zero.
suggestions.risk: Misses timely traffic in the meantime.
suggestions.decide: Hold until Search Console has 2–4 weeks of query data (FLG-009, FLG-020).

suggestions.title: Add a decision log so suggestions are accepted or rejected with a recorded reason and date
suggestions.why: The brief asks for a reviewable path before implementing anything. A log makes each choice auditable, captures why something was rejected, and stops the same suggestion being re-litigated next session.
suggestions.cost: A small table on this page, populated by hand.
suggestions.risk: None. It only records decisions already being made.
suggestions.decide: The decision log now carries dated entries with reasons, including the rejections.

suggestions.title: Ship the seasonal cluster now, and refresh it every November — the position opposite SUG-23
suggestions.why: Seasonal intent is the one demand pattern that does not need a query report to justify: holiday cooking questions arrive every November whether or not we can measure them yet. A shipped seasonal page compounds — it can be re-checked, re-linked, and re-published each year instead of rebuilt. This row was built and shipped under a direct publishing brief; SUG-23 (from the same parallel pass) recommends holding until demand is measured, and both rows are kept so the owner decides rather than either session silently winning.
suggestions.cost: A collection page, a holiday guide, two generated brand images, and a navigation label. Built in this pass.
suggestions.risk: SUG-23 is right that a calendar-driven topic may miss the queries people actually type: no Search Console data exists yet, and the limitation is disclosed on the page itself (FLG-020, Q-23). The risk of shipping was reading as speculative; the mitigation was disclosure, not silence.
suggestions.decide: Shipped this pass. Owner decides at Q-25: adopt the annual November refresh (re-check every linked spec against its source each time), or retire the page in favour of SUG-23\u2019s hold position once real query data exists. Whichever loses is recorded, not deleted.

suggestions.title: Grow the technique cluster by one article a month — jobs, not verdicts
suggestions.why: Technique questions (what to reheat, what to batch, what belongs on the counter) are evergreen, answerable from published specifications, and never require claiming a hands-on test. They are also the cheapest way to close the Associates 10-post bar (FLG-013): this pass added the technique and holiday guides, leaving roughly three additional substantive posts to reach ten on any reading.
suggestions.cost: A guide per month plus its verification pass — the same cost as the weekly cadence in SUG-05 and SUG-21, at a slower, sustainable rate.
suggestions.risk: Ten guides already cover form factor, capacity, cleanup, multi-function, thermometers, technique, holidays, doneness, batching and feature-name literacy. A new article must be a new job (reheating, defrost-and-crisp, batch-prep) or it will restate the same trade-offs and read as filler — the exact failure the brief rejects.
suggestions.decide: Recommend. Start next month if the weekly cadence (SUG-05, SUG-21) is not adopted; if it is, slot technique articles into the same calendar. Each new guide enters the sitemap and feed in the same commit, per the standing rule.

suggestions.title: Expand the brand imagery: one generated counter scene per collection
suggestions.why: The two shipped images cover the seasonal cluster and the guides imagery. A consistent illustration per category (air fryers, thermometers, compare) would make the site read as a publication from any entry page, which is SUG-17\u2019s design-brief requirement made visual.
suggestions.cost: Four generated images and one CSS addition. No ongoing cost.
suggestions.risk: None to compliance as long as the images never depict products, brands, or any appliance that could be mistaken for a listed unit (FLG-007), and each use is labelled on-page. The risk is aesthetic: too many scenes can read as stock.
suggestions.decide: Consider after the seasonal deploy settles. Owner position on generated imagery is Q-26; decide per image, not as a batch, and keep the same warm editorial grade so the set reads as one publication.

suggestions.title: Buy traffic before conversion measurement exists
suggestions.why: Paid acquisition is reasonable only once two things are true: the collector is deployed (FLG-011) so clicks per source are countable, and the Associates tracking report confirms attribution (FLG-004). Neither is true today. Spending before measurement means paying for clicks nobody can trace to an order.
suggestions.cost: Budget, plus the two blockers above.
suggestions.risk: The failure mode is not overspend — it is confidence: unmeasured paid traffic looks identical to organic growth in every report the site currently has.
suggestions.decide: Hold until FLG-011 and FLG-004 close. Re-evaluate in the week after the first Associates report arrives.

suggestions.title: A dedicated head-to-head thermometer page — only when measurement justifies it
suggestions.why: The instant-vs-wireless guide covers the decision narratively. A dedicated side-by-side page would target a different reader — the one who has already decided to compare — and the comparison table already carries the verified spec rows to build it from.
suggestions.cost: One page from existing verified data; no new claims required.
suggestions.risk: It adds another URL competing with the existing guide and compare page for the same intent. Without query data, choosing this topic is instinct — the failure mode SUG-21\u2019s cadence exists to replace.
suggestions.decide: Consider, gated on measurement: build it only if the query report (Q-24) shows thermometer-comparison impressions. Until then the guide and the table cover the intent.

suggestions.title: Draw original line art instead of waiting for photography
suggestions.why: An image-free page is the strongest 'generated' tell left on a site like this, and Program Content (listing images) may not be used without approved tooling. Original schematics are the honest substitute: they are ours, they load instantly, they print, and each one teaches the shape of a decision. This is the position opposite SUG-27 and it needs no owner permission.
suggestions.cost: Done. Each drawing is selected from the product record, so a corrected specification changes the picture with it.
suggestions.risk: A schematic is not the item on your counter. Mitigated by a caption on every drawing and by linking out for real photographs.
suggestions.decide: Shipped 2026-11-20 in _src/art.mjs; every drawing is captioned as a schematic, not a photograph.

suggestions.title: Only advertise a social card when the image file exists
suggestions.why: Every page declared a large social card and pointed at one hard-coded seasonal photograph, and carried a placeholder Search Console token. A site-wide card that is actually a December photo goes stale on the calendar, and a placeholder verification token claims a verification that has not happened.
suggestions.cost: Done: the head template resolves og:image from data (site.socialImage), emits it only when the file is in the tree, and the placeholder token is gone.
suggestions.risk: None. A missing card is a smaller error than a broken or misleading one.
suggestions.decide: Shipped 2026-11-20; closes the placeholder-token half of FLG-025 and feeds Q-26 a per-page hook for imagery.

suggestions.title: If real photography is wanted, licence it — API or brand permission, never scraping
suggestions.why: SUG-27 proposes generated counter scenes, which is a defensible brand choice (Q-26). Photography of the actual items is a different thing and a stronger merchandising asset, but the only compliant sources are Amazon's own creative tooling or written permission from the brand.
suggestions.cost: Blocked on API access (SUG-03) or on a brand licence conversation. No build work until one exists.
suggestions.risk: Scraping or hot-linking listing images breaches the Program Policies and risks the whole account for one jpg.
suggestions.decide: Owner: choose between generated scene-setting art (SUG-27) and licensed photography (this); the site needs at most one of them above the fold.

suggestions.title: Put the front page in front of five real readers before adding another guide
suggestions.why: There is no traffic yet, so there is no behavioural data. A short moderated read test is the only substitute, and it answers the one question a redesign cannot: does a stranger know what to do next within fifteen seconds?
suggestions.cost: Five people, ten minutes each, one question after the first screen.
suggestions.risk: A small sample tells you about comprehension, not about demand. Do not read it as validation.
suggestions.decide: Owner: run it, or skip to the collector and read clicks instead (Q-27).

suggestions.title: Close the parallel duplicate-site pull requests before another session builds on them
suggestions.why: Several open pull requests add competing root-level sites, each with its own homepage, stylesheet, dashboard and feed. Merging any of them alongside the current build recreates the duplicate-content failure this board records twice, and forks the compliance gate into two divergent copies.
suggestions.cost: A review pass per PR: take the verified data rows, decline the second site.
suggestions.risk: Closing a session's work feels wasteful. The archive convention already preserves it without serving it.
suggestions.decide: Owner decision (Q-29). Nothing on this branch merged, edited or closed any of them.

designBrief.intro: A draft design brief to feed a design prompt. These are recommendations for the visual and editorial direction of the site, not verified facts. They exist so the site can read as a polished marketing publication rather than a templated generated site. Each principle names the constraint it respects, where one applies.

principles.principle: Use an opinionated editorial type system: a serif display face for headlines and a clean sans for body, set in a clear hierarchy with generous line height and a readable measure.
principles.why: A confident type system reads as a real publication. Uniform system-font stacks with flat sizing read as generated.
principles.constraint: None. Keep contrast and a readable line length, especially on mobile.

principles.principle: Use a restrained, limited palette with one accent color. Avoid generic blue-to-purple gradients and neon highlights.
principles.why: Gradients and neon are among the most common visual tells of AI-generated marketing pages. Restraint reads as intentional.

principles.principle: Do not use emoji or icons as decoration. Use a real icon set only where it carries meaning.
principles.why: Emoji-as-decoration is a strong tell of generated content and looks unprofessional on a buying guide.

principles.principle: Vary section layouts: a strong editorial hero, a reading column for guides, and at least one non-card treatment per page. Do not repeat the identical card grid in every section.
principles.why: Repeated identical cards are a primary tell of templated generation. Variation reads as designed.
principles.constraint: Mobile-first; keep tables and cards readable.

principles.principle: Keep the disclosure strip and sponsored labels exactly where policy requires, and design around them rather than treating them as an afterthought.
principles.why: Disclosure placement is a compliance requirement, not a style choice.
principles.constraint: FTC Disclosures 101 (hard to miss); Associates Operating Agreement §5.

principles.principle: Write in a concrete, human, opinionated voice using specifics and named trade-offs. Ban filler phrases and generic marketing boilerplate.
principles.why: Specificity reads human and is what helpful-content guidance rewards; filler is the other main slop tell.
principles.constraint: FTC: no experience you do not have. The Associate statement stays verbatim.

source.label: Google Search Central — Creating Helpful Content

principles.principle: Until compliant product imagery is available, keep the site typographic: color, type and a defined illustration or pattern system carry the design. Do not hot-link, store, or substitute Amazon imagery, and do not use stock photos of a different appliance.
principles.why: Unlicensed or misrepresenting imagery would violate program policy and mislead the reader. A confident typographic system can look polished without photos.
principles.constraint: Participation Requirements §6(a); IP License. See FLG-007.

principles.principle: Make the sponsored status of every outbound product link visible at the link, and keep the Associate statement above the fold on every page.
principles.why: Reader trust and FTC disclosure both require the material connection to be visible where the endorsement happens.
principles.constraint: FTC 16 CFR 255.5; Associates OA §5; Program Policies.

topicRoadmap.note: Editorial hypotheses only. None of these titles is a claim about search volume, popularity, or product superiority. Selection is a draft for a publishing cadence; which topics earn traffic is decided by measured query data once Search Console is verified (FLG-009, FLG-020), not by instinct.

decisionLog.note: Every entry below mirrors a decision already written into the register above, with the reason that was written at the time. Accepted items are already in the build; adopted items are decided but not yet built. Recommended and open items are the project's written position and still need the owner's acceptance; held and rejected items stay recorded so they are not re-litigated. A new decision is appended with its own date rather than editing an old row. Rows are one per suggestion, and a suggestion whose status is Shipped must read Accepted here — the compliance gate checks the pairing, so this log cannot quietly disagree with the register.

decisionKey.label: Accepted
decisionKey.note: Written as accepted and already built into the live site.

decisionKey.label: Adopted
decisionKey.note: Decided, with the date and the basis, but not yet built. Nothing is published by the decision itself.

decisionKey.label: Recommended
decisionKey.note: The project's written recommendation, with the reasoning and the risk. Not yet accepted by the owner.

decisionKey.label: Open
decisionKey.note: No recommendation to build yet: it needs an earlier decision, a credential, or a person.

decisionKey.label: Hold
decisionKey.note: Deliberately not now, with the condition that would unblock it.

decisionKey.label: Rejected
decisionKey.note: Will not be built. Recorded so a later session does not build it in good faith.

rubric: Answer the blocking questions first (Q-04 enrolment, Q-09 testing, Q-16 measurement).
Score each suggestion: impact × confidence ÷ cost.
Read the risk column before accepting; a suggestion that needs a credential is gated, not blocked.
Accept or reject in writing, with a one-line reason and a date.
Re-review quarterly against measured data, not instinct.
killCriteria: A topic with no measured demand after four weeks is dropped, not padded.
A suggestion whose risk has grown (for example it would breach policy) is moved to rejected.
No new topic is added from instinct while the query report is empty.

entries.reason: Accepted and already live: every page writes about the decision instead of a verdict, because no product in this register has been tested.
One site, air fryers in front, thermometers as the second section — which is the structure already in place. Confirm before a third category is added.
Apply as soon as the account qualifies. Eligibility depends on qualifying sales first, so it stays tracked as Q-11 and Q-12.

Basis: Associates Help 'Application Review Process' (FLG-013). This sets the schedule only; no new guide is published by this decision. Week-eight measurement waits on owner-connected Search Console and analytics (FLG-009, FLG-011).
Recommended, and it needs a real, named person who is accountable for the writing. A byline cannot be fabricated, so this waits on the owner.

The About page already carries this, and the front page deliberately keeps process notes off the reader's path.

Near-duplicate pages to chase long-tail queries are what this publication exists not to be; the build gate refuses pages without unique content.

Shipped 2026-11-20: the front page alternates hero, shopper router, card shelf, seasonal banner, guide cards and an honesty line; the category hubs gained a shelf list view instead of repeating the grid.

The topic roadmap below is the first batch of hypotheses; measured demand reorders it later, never the other way round.

designPrompt.intro: A ready-to-use design prompt for the visual redesign. The goal is a polished marketing affiliate publication — not a templated, AI-generated shop. It consolidates the design brief (DB-01 to DB-08) and the compliance constraints so a designer, or an AI design prompt, has a single source to act on. Nothing here is a verified fact; it is a recommendation awaiting a decision in the decision log.
designPrompt.prompt: Design Counter Space, a polished marketing affiliate publication about kitchen gear. Visual direction: an opinionated editorial type system — serif display headlines, clean sans body, generous line height, readable measure. Restrained palette with one accent color; no blue-to-purple gradients, no neon highlights, no emoji or decorative icons. Vary section layouts — a strong editorial hero, a reading column for guides, at least one non-card treatment per page; do not repeat the identical card grid everywhere. Keep the disclosure strip above the fold on every page and the Sponsored label on every outbound product link; these are compliance requirements, not afterthoughts. Write in a concrete, human voice using specifics and named trade-offs; ban filler phrases and generic marketing boilerplate. Until compliant product imagery is available, keep the site typographic: color, type and an illustration or pattern system carry the design. Do not hot-link, store, or substitute Amazon imagery, and do not use stock photos of a different appliance. Meet WCAG contrast and stay readable on mobile, especially tables and cards. HTML/CSS only; no third-party analytics or tracking scripts.
constraints: FTC Disclosures 101 — disclosure hard to miss, placed with the endorsement
Associates Operating Agreement §5 — verbatim Associate statement above the fold
Program Policies §6(a) and IP License — no unlicensed or misrepresenting imagery
FTC 16 CFR 255.5 — sponsored status visible at the link
Google Search Central helpful-content — concrete human voice, no filler

paths.note: Three coherent ways forward, in order. Each is a sequence, not a menu: a step is only worth doing once the step before it is done, and steps marked blocked are blocked on an account, not on a decision we can make here. The pick is recorded so the choice is explicit.
paths.why: Path A is picked because it is the only path that can be finished without a credential, and it removes the two things a buyer notices first: a front page that opened with audit counters, and a publication with no imagery at all. Path B is worth more and is listed next, unfinished on purpose, because it belongs to whoever holds the Associates login. The seasonal cluster that a parallel session shipped is folded into Path A step 4 rather than treated as a competing plan.

options.name: Make it presentable, then make it measurable
options.oneLiner: Ship the reader-facing polish that needs no access, then turn on measurement and let the data pick the next topic.

steps.text: Adopt the written design brief and implement it: type scale, contrast, layout variation
Replace the audit counters above the products with a shopper router
Draw original schematics in place of the photography the program will not let us use
Publish the roadmap titles and put them in the sitemap and feed in the same commit
Verify the property in Search Console and submit the sitemap
Deploy the collector so the five defined events actually record
At week eight, replace the topic hypotheses with measured queries

options.unlocks: One indexable site that reads as published rather than generated, and a reader-facing surface a person can judge in fifteen seconds.
options.cost: Repository work only for the first four steps; the last three need the owner's accounts.
options.risk: Polish without authority does not create traffic. Which is why this path ends in measurement instead of in more pages.
options.firstSignal: Impressions for guide queries in Search Console, or a non-empty day bucket from the collector.

options.name: Prove the money path first
options.oneLiner: Before anything else grows, confirm the account, the tag and one real click per product.

steps.text: Confirm shopnow047c-20 is enrolled and that the registered site URL matches this deployment
Build one Special Link per product in Associates Central, click it logged out, record the destination and the next day's reporting line
Open the five submitted short links in a logged-out browser and reconcile them against the register
Decide whether the supplied short links stay anywhere on the site at all

options.unlocks: Attribution confidence. Without it the site is a shop that cannot be shown to earn, and every later optimisation is guesswork.
options.cost: About half an hour in a browser with the account open. No code changes.
options.risk: Nothing in doing it; everything in skipping it. No other path can report orders until this one closes.
options.firstSignal: A click in the Associates click report within 48 hours, then an order line.

options.name: Build the merchandising layer
options.oneLiner: API pricing, ratings, licensed imagery and email capture — all of which depend on access and on measured demand.

steps.text: Qualify for Product Advertising / Creatives API access, which requires qualifying sales first
Show prices and ratings from the API only, with the refresh interval documented on the page
Replace schematics with licensed or generated imagery, once the owner has picked which
Turn on reader capture once there is something worth sending
Extend the seasonal page into a calendar once measured demand justifies it

options.unlocks: Real merchandising: current prices, star ratings, product photography, and a list you own.
options.cost: Account qualification, then API plumbing and a refresh job. Weeks, not hours.
options.risk: Building a data pipeline on unmeasured demand — and any price shown must come from the API or the program is breached.
options.firstSignal: One PA-API response returning a live price for one of the five ASINs.
